questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a paramagnetic bar is brought near a bar magnet, then it is
options: Attracted by both the poles of the bar magnet
Repelled by both the poles of the bar magnet
Attracted by the South-pole and repelled by the North-pole of the bar magnet
Attracted by the North-pole and repelled by the South-pole of the bar magnet
questions.solution:
Paramagnetic materials have a tendency to move from a region of weak magnetic field to a region of strong magnetic field.

When a paramagnetic bar is brought near either pole of a bar magnet, it gets weakly magnetized in the direction of the external magnetic field.

This induced magnetization causes the near end of the bar to develop an opposite magnetic polarity to that of the adjacent pole of the bar magnet.

Therefore, the paramagnetic bar is attracted by both the North and South poles of the bar magnet.

Answer: Attracted by both the poles of the bar magnet

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Pick out the WRONG statements about magnetic substances.
(\chi$ = magnetic susceptibility)
(\mu_r$ = relative permeability).
I. Substances with $-1 \leq \chi < 0$ are diamagnetic.
II. Substances with $\chi \gg 1$ are paramagnetic.
III. Substances with $\chi \ll 1$ are ferromagnetic.
IV. Substances with $\mu_r \gg 1$ are ferromagnetic.
questions.solution:
For diamagnetic substances, the magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ is small and negative, so $-1 \leq \chi < 0$. Statement I is correct.

For paramagnetic substances, $\chi$ is small and positive, so $0 < \chi < \epsilon$. Statement II states $\chi \gg 1$, which is incorrect as this condition applies to ferromagnetic substances.

For ferromagnetic substances, $\chi$ is very large and positive, so $\chi \gg 1$. Statement III states $\chi \ll 1$, which is incorrect.

For ferromagnetic substances, the relative permeability $\mu_r = 1 + \chi$. Since $\chi \gg 1$, it follows that $\mu_r \gg 1$. Statement IV is correct.

Therefore, statements II and III are wrong.

Answer: II and III

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Magnetic susceptibility of Mg at 300 K is $1.2 \times 10^{-5}$. What is its susceptibility at $200 \mathrm{ K} ?$
questions.solution:
We know that magnetic susceptibility.
$\chi \propto \frac{1}{T}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\chi_2}{\chi_1}=\frac{T_1}{T_2} \Rightarrow \chi_2=\frac{T_1}{T_2} \times \chi_1=1.2 \times 10^{-5} \times \frac{300}{200}=1.8 \times 10^{-5}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The Curie temperature of cobalt and iron are $1400 \mathrm{ K}$ and $1000 \mathrm{ K}$ respectively. At $T=1600 \mathrm{ K}$, the ratio of magnetic susceptibility of cobalt to that of iron is
questions.solution:
$We know that, magnetic susceptibility,
\begin{aligned} & \chi=\frac{C}{T-T_C} \\ \therefore \quad & \chi \propto \frac{1}{T-T_C}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \frac{\chi_{\text{cobalt }}}{\chi_{\text{iron }}} & =\frac{T-\left(T_C\right)_{\text{iron }}}{T-\left(T_C\right)_{\text{cobalt }}} \\ & =\frac{1600-1000}{1600-1400}=\frac{600}{200}=3\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Earth's magnetic field always has a horizontal component except at
questions.solution:
At poles magnetic dip, $\delta=90^{{}^{\circ}}$
As, horizontal component of Earth's magnetic field,
$B_{H}=B \cos \delta$
where, $B$ is net earth's magnetic field.
$\Rightarrow \quad B_{H}=B \cos 90^{{}^{\circ}}=0$
So, at poles, the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the field pattern given below is valid for electric field as well as for magnetic field?
questions.solution:
Option (a) and (b) represents electric field lines due to positive and negative charges. However, magnetic monopoles does not exist in nature.
So, option (a) and (b) is not correct for magnetic field lines.
Option (c) represents magnetic field lines for current carrying conductor.
Also, electric field lines cannot form closed loop. So, option (c) is incorrect.
Option (d) is possible for magnetic field lines of solenoid and electric field lines of dipole.
Thus, option (d) is valid for both electric and magnetic field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A paramagnetic sample shows a net magnetisation of $8 \mathrm{Am}^{-1}$ when placed in an external magnetic field of $0.6 \mathrm{ T}$ at a temperature of $4 \mathrm{ K}$. When the same sample is placed in an external magnetic field of $0.2 \mathrm{ T}$ at a temperature of $16 \mathrm{ K}$, the magnetisation will be
questions.solution:
Given, $M_{1}=8 \mathrm{Am}^{-1}, B_{1}=0.6 \mathrm{ T}, T_{1}=4 \mathrm{ K}$, $B_{2}=0.2 \mathrm{ T}$ and $T_{2}=16 \mathrm{ K}$
According to Curie's law, for paramagnetic materials,
$M=\frac{C B}{T}\Rightarrow \quad M_{1}=\frac{C B_{1}}{T_{1}}$
and $\quad M_{2}=\frac{C B_{2}}{T_{2}}\therefore \quad \frac{M_{2}}{M_{1}} \frac{\frac{C B_{2}}{T_{2}}}{\frac{C B_{1}}{T_{1}}}=\frac{B_{2}}{B_{1}} \times \frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}=\frac{0.2}{0.6} \times \frac{4 \mathrm{ K}}{16 \mathrm{ K}}=\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{4}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{M_{2}}{M_{1}}=\frac{1}{12} \Rightarrow M_{2}=\frac{M_{1}}{12}=\frac{8}{12}\Rightarrow \quad M_{2}=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{Am}^{-1}$

Substituting values in Eq. $(1)$, we get
$e=2 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000 \times 25=5 \mathrm{ V}$

questions.q:
\( x_{1} \) and \( x_{2} \) are susceptibility of a paramagnetic material at temperatures \( T_{1} K \) and \( T_{2} K \)
respectively, then
questions.solution:
Susceptibility is a dimensionless number. It is a measure of the extent to which a substance becomes magnetized.
Paramagnetic susceptibility \( \chi \) is given as
\[ $\begin{array}{l} \chi=\frac{N g^{2} \beta^{2} S(S+1)}{3 K T}\\ \Rightarrow \chi \propto \frac{1}{T} \text{ or } \chi T \propto 1 \end{array}$ \]
Therefore \( \chi_{1} T_{1}=\chi_{2} T_{2} \)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
At certain place, the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field is \( 3.0 $\mathrm{G}$\) and the angle dip
at that place is \( 30^{{}^{\circ}} \). The magnetic field of earth at that location
questions.solution:
Given, horizontal component of Earth's magnetic field $=3.0 \mathrm{G} ;$ angle of dip $=30^{{}^{\circ}}$
Now, horizontal component = B $\cos$ (angle of dip)
$\Rightarrow 3.0 G=B \cos 30^{{}^{\circ}}\Rightarrow B=\frac{3.0}{\cos 30^{{}^{\circ}}}=\frac{3.0 \times 2}{\sqrt{3}}\Rightarrow B=2 \sqrt{3}=3.464 \sim 3.5 \mathrm{G}$
Therefore, magnetic field of Earth at that location $=3.5 \mathrm{G}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Two coils have a mutual inductance \( 0.005 $\mathrm{H}$\). The current changes in the first coil according to
the equation \( i=i_{m} \sin \omega t \) where \( i_{m}=10 $\mathrm{ A}$\) and \(\omega=100 \Pi $\mathrm{rad} \mathrms^{-1}$\). The maximum value of
the emf induced in the second coil is
questions.solution:
Given, mutual inductance,
\( M=0.005 H ; i=i_{\omega} \sin \omega t ; i_{m}=10 A ; \omega=100 \pi r a d s^{-1} \)
Then emf induced is
\( \varepsilon=M $\frac{d I}{d t}=$M $\frac{d}{d t}\left($i_{m} \sin \omega t\right)=M i_{m} \omega \cos \omega t \)
Maximum value of emf is obtained when \( \cos \omega t=1 \).
Therefore \( \varepsilon_{\max }=M \omega i_{m}=0.005 \times10 \times100 \Pi=5 \Pi \)
Thus, maximum value of emf induced in the second coil is \( 5 \pi\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An aircraft with a wingspan of \( 40 $\mathrm{ m}$\) flies with a speed of \( 1080 $\mathrm{ km} \mathrm{ h}^{-1}$\) in the eastward
direction at a constant altitude in the northern hemisphere, where the vertical component of the
earth's magnetic field \( 1.75 \times10^{-5} $\mathrm{ T}$\). Then the emf developed between the tips of the wings is
questions.solution:
Given, length of wing, $l=40 \mathrm{ m}$; speed, $v=1080 \mathrm{kmh}^{-1}=1080 \times \frac{5}{18} \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$
Earth's magnetic field,$B=1.75 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{ T}$
Then emf
$E=B l v=\left(1.75 \times 10^{-5}\right) \times 40 \times 1080 \times \frac{5}{18}=21000 \times 10^{-5}=0.21 \mathrm{ V}$
Therefore, the emf developed between the tips of the wing is $0.21 \mathrm{ V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A solenoid has length \( 0.4 $\mathrm{ cm}$\), radius \( 1 $\mathrm{ cm}$\) and \( 400 \) turns of wire. If a current of \( 5 $\mathrm{ A}$\) is passed
through this solenoid, what is the magnetic field inside the solenoid?
questions.solution:
Given, length of solenoid $=0.4 \mathrm{ cm}=0.4 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{ m} ;$ radius $=1 \mathrm{ cm}=10^{-2} \mathrm{ m} ;$ number of turns $=400 ;$ current
through solenoid $=5 \mathrm{ A}$.
Therefore, magnetic field inside solenoid $=\mu_{0} n I=4 \Pi \times 10^{-7} \times \frac{400}{0.4 \times 10^{-2}} \times 5=0.628 \mathrm{ T}$

questions.solution:
For tangent galvanometer

$\begin{aligned}$I &=K \tan $\theta$\\
K &=$\frac{I}{\tan \theta}$\\
K &=$\frac{2 / \sqrt{3}}{\tan 60^{{}^{\circ}}}$\\
K &=$\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{~A}
\end{aligned}$
